name: Underwrite mid-ticket credit applications
summary: Applications above $250,000, or that take a customer's total exposure above that level, go to eight senior analysts who underwrite them from financial statements rather than from bureau scores alone. An analyst screens the package, chases missing statements, searches registrations, spreads the statements, analyses cash flow, guarantors, industry and management, asks asset management to value used or specialised equipment and writes a credit memo with a recommended structure. The mid-ticket manager approves within authority and passes larger exposures to the director of credit and, beyond that, to the chief credit officer or committee. Waiting for customers' statements, valuations and approvers stretches the cycle to days or weeks while competitors quote the same deal.

baseline.org_archetype: A mid-size privately owned Canadian independent equipment lessor underwriting about 430 mid-ticket applications a month (average funded deal about $380,000) with eight senior analysts, a manager and the director of credit.
baseline.notes: Spreading in spreadsheets, memos in word processing attached to the origination portal, laddered delegated authority; a lighter review track for strong profiles at the low end of mid-ticket.

trigger: A set-up application above $250,000 (or above that level of total exposure), a fraud-cleared file, an appeal or a returned higher-authority decision enters the mid-ticket queue.
end_state: A credit decision (approval with structure and conditions, or decline) is released to the account executive or broker, or the file is withdrawn for missing statements or submitted to the chief credit officer or committee.

volume.seasonality: Busier in spring and before calendar year end when customers time capital spending; statements are slow to arrive during tax season and around fiscal year ends.

evidence.note: From the organisation's process map: about 13% of 3,430 applications a month, plus appeals and returned decisions.

Duties from a Canadian lessor's mid-ticket senior analyst posting; organisation file cost (upper part of NOC 11109, loaded x1.35, scaled to 2019-2022). About 7.6 of the 8 analysts' time; the rest goes to annual reviews of large exposures (review-large-exposures).
Organisation file cost (NOC 10021). About three quarters of the manager's time goes to assigning files and approving memos within authority (tier C share).
Mid-ticket analysts report to the director of credit per the posting; about a third of the director's time goes to mid-ticket approvals (tier C share).
Asset managers' valuation work is documented in the value-equipment-and-set-residuals process; this workflow records only the wait for it, so no time is counted here.

systems.name: Vendor and broker application portal with origination workflow and document generation
Lease management system (contracts, schedules, billing, tax codes, asset records, servicing)
Commercial and consumer credit bureau portals (Equifax, PayNet)
Provincial personal property registry and Quebec RDPRM search and registration portals
Spreadsheet models (pool cuts, borrowing base, covenants, budget, tax workpapers)
Document imaging and contract file store

steps.name: File arrives in mid-ticket credit
steps.description: A file reaches mid-ticket credit as a newly set-up application above $250,000 or with total exposure above that level, as a file cleared by the fraud analyst, as an appeal or restructure request from sales, or back from the chief credit officer or credit committee with a decision.

evidence.note: Shares estimated from the organisation file's volumes: about 380 routed applications, 10 fraud clearances, 15 appeals and 30 returned decisions a month.

steps.name: Manager assigns file to an analyst
steps.description: The mid-ticket credit manager reviews new files at the morning huddle and assigns each to a senior analyst by workload, industry knowledge and the originator's relationship, marking competitive or time-sensitive deals.

evidence.note: Tier C estimate from the author's knowledge of mid-ticket credit at independent lessors; assignment once or twice a day.

steps.name: Analyst screens file and document package
steps.description: The analyst reads the set-up summary, bureau reports and exposure, sizes the request against the customer's revenue, and checks the package for two years of financial statements with interims, tax returns where statements are not reviewed, guarantors' net worth statements, a debt schedule and the supplier quote. Obvious policy failures are declined early.
outputs: screening result and list of missing documents

error.defect_description: A missing interim statement is not noticed until the memo is drafted.

control.basis: Credit policy financial information requirements by deal size (statements, interims, tax returns and net worth statements above $250,000)

evidence.note: Document requirements above $250,000 are documented; analysts carry several files so new ones wait one to three days; shares are tier C.

steps.name: Request financial statements and documents
steps.description: The analyst emails the account executive or broker a list of what is still needed, such as the latest interim statements, the accountant's year-end statements, tax returns, guarantors' net worth statements or an aging of receivables, and sets a follow-up date.

evidence.note: The documents required are listed by a lessor; times are tier C.

steps.name: Customer and accountant provide documents
steps.description: The customer asks its accountant for statements or interim figures and gathers tax returns and net worth statements, which the account executive or broker forwards. This often takes several days, especially near year end or tax season, and some customers give up or finance elsewhere.

next.condition: documents never arrive or deal is lost

evidence.note: Tier C estimate from the author's knowledge of mid-ticket credit at independent lessors; one to ten days; the organisation file names waiting for statements as the main delay.

steps.name: Search registrations against the customer
steps.description: The analyst searches the personal property registry in the customer's province, or Quebec's RDPRM, for existing security interests, such as a bank's general security agreement or another lessor's registration on the same equipment, and notes anything that affects priority or signals hidden debt.

error.defect_description: A prior registration on the same serial number is missed.

control.basis: Credit policy: confirm existing secured creditors and the lessor's priority under the provincial PPSA or Quebec Civil Code before approval

next.condition: streamlined review for a strong profile up to about $500,000

evidence.note: Registration and priority rules are statutory; the search at underwriting and the streamlined share are tier C.

steps.name: Streamlined review and short-form memo
steps.description: For established customers with strong bureau and payment history and deals up to about $500,000, the analyst reviews the statements without a full spread, checks revenue, profit and leverage trends, uses the residual table for the equipment and writes a short-form memo with risk rating and recommended structure, deciding it alone when it is within the senior analyst's authority.

error.defect_description: Weak trend or hidden debt missed in the lighter review.

next.condition: within the senior analyst's own approval authority

evidence.note: Tier C estimate from the author's knowledge of mid-ticket credit at independent lessors; many lessors keep a lighter track for the lower end of mid-ticket and give senior analysts authority for it.

steps.name: Spread financial statements
steps.description: The analyst types two or three years of balance sheets and income statements, plus interims, into the spreading spreadsheet, maps accounts to standard lines, adjusts for owner compensation and one-time items and checks that the spread balances.

error.defect_description: Keying or mapping error in the spread that distorts ratios.

evidence.note: Spreadsheet spreading and its errors are documented; times are tier C.

steps.name: Analyse cash flow and debt service coverage
steps.description: The analyst calculates cash flow available for debt service, adds the proposed lease payments to existing debt, computes coverage and leverage, combines related companies and guarantors where they support the deal and tests what happens if revenue falls.

error.defect_description: Existing lease or loan payments left out of debt service.

evidence.note: Repayment capacity and debt service coverage analysis are documented practice; times are tier C.

steps.name: Assess guarantors' personal net worth
steps.description: The analyst reviews each guarantor's personal net worth statement against the personal bureau report, discounts illiquid assets and notes contingent liabilities, and judges how much support the guarantees really add.

evidence.note: Guarantor analysis and owners' financial statements are documented; times are tier C.

steps.name: Review industry, management and concentration
steps.description: The analyst researches the industry outlook, the company's customers and contracts, management's experience and any concentration on one customer or project, using the company's overview, web sources and the account executive's notes.

next.condition: management call or site visit needed

evidence.note: Industry overview and qualitative factors are documented memo content; shares are tier C.

steps.name: Hold management call or site visit
steps.description: The analyst and the account executive schedule a call, or for larger deals a visit, with the owner to understand the business, the reason for the equipment, upcoming contracts and anything unusual in the statements.

evidence.note: Analysts negotiate structure by phone with lessees; scheduling times are tier C.

steps.name: Request equipment valuation
steps.description: For used, specialised or high-value equipment, or a fair market value lease with a large residual, the analyst sends asset management a valuation request with the make, model, year, hours, invoice and proposed term.

evidence.note: Tier C estimate from the author's knowledge of mid-ticket credit at independent lessors; a short request form.

steps.name: Wait for asset management valuation
steps.description: An asset manager values the equipment from auction and dealer data or orders a third-party appraisal or inspection and returns current value, a recommended advance and a residual. The asset manager's work is part of the valuation process; this step is the analyst's wait for it.

evidence.note: Third-party appraisals take 7 to 15 business days desktop; internal desktop valuations are faster (tier C).

steps.name: Draft credit memo and recommend structure
steps.description: The analyst writes the credit memo: request and recommendation, borrower and management, industry, financial analysis and coverage, collateral value and advance, guarantors, risk rating, policy exceptions and the recommended structure such as term, down payment, security deposit, residual and reporting covenants.

error.defect_description: Recommendation and conditions in the memo do not match the analysis.

evidence.note: Memo contents are documented; times are tier C.

steps.name: Revise memo after review
steps.description: The analyst reworks the memo after the manager or director asks for changes, or after an appeal: re-running coverage with a new structure, adding conditions, answering the approver's questions or updating figures, then sends it back for review.

evidence.note: Recreating proposals after approvers' recommendations is documented; times are tier C.

steps.name: Manager reviews and approves memo
steps.description: The mid-ticket credit manager reads the memo and spread, challenges assumptions and structure with the analyst, and approves or declines within the manager's authority, sends the memo back for rework or more information, or recommends it to the director of credit.

control.basis: Delegated credit authority: manager approval limit by exposure and risk rating, with a second signature for amounts above it

evidence.note: Approval limits commensurate with amount and risk are documented; times and shares are tier C.

steps.name: Director of credit reviews and approves
steps.description: The director of credit reviews memos above the manager's limit, often asking for changes to the structure or extra conditions, and approves or declines within the director's authority or sends the largest and most complex exposures on to the chief credit and risk officer or the credit committee.

control.basis: Delegated credit authority: director approval limit set by the board-approved authority matrix

evidence.note: Laddered authority and analysts reporting to a director of credit are documented; times are tier C.

steps.name: Record decision and conditions
steps.description: The analyst enters the decision, risk rating, approved structure, expiry date and conditions precedent such as guarantees, insurance, registration, annual financial statements or a security deposit in the portal, attaches the signed memo and logs any policy exception.

error.defect_description: A condition is left off, so documents are prepared without it.

control.basis: Credit policy documentation standard and exception tracking

evidence.note: Documentation and exception tracking are documented practice; the approval share is tier C.

steps.name: Release approval to originator
steps.description: The portal posts the approval, conditions and expiry to the account executive or broker desk, which takes it to the customer.

next.condition: approved with conditions or a changed structure

evidence.note: Approvals are valid for a set period; the condition share is tier C.

steps.name: Release decline to originator
steps.description: The portal posts the decline and its reasons to the account executive or broker desk, which tells the customer and may come back with a restructure request.

evidence.note: Tier C estimate from the author's knowledge of mid-ticket credit at independent lessors; automatic portal notice.

steps.name: Write early decline rationale
steps.description: When the screen shows a clear policy failure, such as losses in both years, a recent insolvency or an exposure the company will not take, the analyst writes a short decline rationale and records it for the manager's sign-off in the daily list.

evidence.note: Tier C estimate from the author's knowledge of mid-ticket credit at independent lessors; a short note.

steps.name: Review appeal or restructure request
steps.description: The analyst reads the request from the account executive or broker, for example a larger down payment, a shorter term, an added guarantor or new interim figures, updates the analysis and either revises the memo or takes the change straight to the manager.

next.condition: change taken straight to the manager

evidence.note: Structural changes negotiated with brokers and lessees are documented; times are tier C.

steps.name: Record higher-authority decision
steps.description: When the chief credit and risk officer or the credit committee returns a decision, the analyst records it with any added conditions in the portal so it can be released.

error.defect_description: An added condition is not transcribed.

evidence.note: Tier C estimate from the author's knowledge of mid-ticket credit at independent lessors; a short transcription.

steps.name: Prepare submission for chief credit officer or committee
steps.description: The analyst turns the memo into the committee format with the director's comments, a summary of total exposure, the risk rating rationale and the exceptions, and sends it for the next decision by the chief credit and risk officer or the credit committee.

control.basis: Board-approved authority matrix: exposures above the director's limit go to the chief credit and risk officer or the credit committee

evidence.note: Committee approval for larger amounts and re-formatting proposals for committee are documented; times are tier C.

exceptions.name: Missing financial statements
exceptions.description: Statements, interims, tax returns or net worth statements are missing; the analyst waits days for the customer's accountant and about one file in five is never completed.

exceptions.name: Equipment valuation needed
exceptions.description: Used, specialised or high-residual equipment is valued by asset management, sometimes through a third-party appraisal that takes one to three weeks.

exceptions.name: Escalated to the director
exceptions.description: Exposures above the manager's limit go to the director of credit, who often adds conditions or changes the structure.

exceptions.name: Submitted above the director's authority
exceptions.description: The largest or most complex exposures go to the chief credit and risk officer or credit committee and come back later as returned decisions.

exceptions.name: Memo rework
exceptions.description: The manager or director sends the memo back for changes to the analysis, structure or conditions.

exceptions.name: Early decline
exceptions.description: The screen shows a clear policy failure and the file is declined without full underwriting.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from entering mid-ticket credit to decision released
benchmarks.population: Mid-ticket credit at Canadian independent lessors, 2019-2022

evidence.note: Once a complete package is in hand a decision can come within a business day (Crest Capital), but analyst backlogs, missing statements, valuations and approver availability make three to five calendar days typical and two weeks or more common for files waiting on statements or appraisals. No published distribution was found.

benchmarks.population: A US lessor for transactions above $250,000

evidence.note: Stated typical time once the full financial package is in.

benchmarks.population: A US equipment appraiser serving lenders

evidence.note: Applies to the share of valuations sent to outside appraisers.

benchmarks.unit: deal size above which financial statements are required
benchmarks.population: A Canadian broker network ($80,000) and a US lessor ($250,000)

evidence.note: Sources disagree; this organisation uses $250,000.
430 applications for eight analysts; only about a third get a full spread and memo.

pain_points.description: Waiting for customers' financial statements, interims and net worth statements is the longest delay, and many files stall or are lost to competitors in the meantime.

evidence.note: The organisation file names this as the main delay.

pain_points.description: Spreading in spreadsheets is slow and error-prone, and analysts calculate ratios differently, which the manager has to catch on review.

evidence.note: Spreadsheet errors and inconsistent calculations are documented.

pain_points.description: Files wait in analysts' backlogs and for the manager and director, who review memos between their own meetings and files.

evidence.note: Committee and laddered approval slow responsiveness; queue times are tier C.

pain_points.description: Valuations for used and specialised equipment, especially outside appraisals, add days to weeks.

evidence.note: Appraisal turnaround of 7 to 25 business days is published.

pain_points.description: Memos are re-formatted for committee and re-worked after approvers change the structure.

evidence.note: Recreating proposals after committee recommendations is documented.

sources.title: Equipment leasing over $250,000
sources.supports: Above $250,000 a lessor asks for a company overview, the equipment's purpose and justification, the last two year-end financial statements and current interims, two years of tax returns unless statements are reviewed or audited, returns and a financial statement for owners of 20% or more and a list of current loans and leases; once the full package is in, an answer typically comes within a business day.

sources.title: Senior Credit Analyst, Bennington Financial (job posting)
sources.supports: A Canadian equipment lessor's senior credit analyst handles mid-ticket adjudication of $250,000 and up and complex deals, recommends acceptance, pricing and structure, reads financial statements in depth, negotiates structure with brokers and lessees by phone and reports to the director of credit; 10+ years' experience asked.

sources.title: Comptroller's Handbook: Loan Portfolio Management (April 1998, updated June 2017)
sources.publisher: Office of the Comptroller of the Currency
sources.supports: Underwriting standards include current and historical balance sheet and income data, projections and financial analysis including repayment capacity; loan authorities should be commensurate with experience and the type, amount and risk of credit, with group or committee approval for larger amounts; the committee method slows responsiveness while individual signature authority is more timely.

sources.title: Commercial credit analysis 101: back to basics
sources.supports: A credit memo should be two pages or less with a customer overview and recommendation, risk score, terms, pricing and covenants, key financials and ratios, an industry overview and policy exceptions, supported by global cash flow, guarantor and collateral analysis; debt service coverage compares expected income with recurring debt payments.

sources.title: Sageworks Credit Analysis product sheet
sources.supports: Lenders spreading in spreadsheets face errors, calculations that differ between analysts, time-consuming global cash flow analysis and proposals recreated after loan committee recommendations.

sources.title: Equipment appraisals
sources.supports: Third-party equipment appraisals for lenders take 7 to 15 business days desktop and 15 to 25 business days on site, on fair market, orderly liquidation and forced liquidation value premises.

sources.title: Personal Property Security Act [RSBC 1996] chapter 359
sources.supports: The Act applies to a lease for a term of more than one year; registration of a financing statement perfects a security interest; a purchase-money security interest perfected within 15 days of possession has priority over other security interests in the same collateral.

sources.title: Marlin Business Services Corp. Form 10-K for fiscal year 2019
sources.supports: Transactions over $150,000 receive a higher level of scrutiny which may include a review of financial statements; approvals are typically valid for up to 90 days.

sources.title: EasyLease: equipment and vendor leasing
sources.supports: A Canadian leasing broker network requires two years of financial statements plus interims from $80,000 for businesses over two years old, and a personal net worth statement for younger businesses.

sources.title: Equifax Business Credit Report user guide
sources.supports: Commercial report scores and trade, collection, legal and inquiry detail used in credit review.

sources.title: Wages: Finance and credit administrator in Ontario (NOC 11109)
sources.supports: Ontario hourly wages low $23.00, median $36.92, high $66.46 (2023-2024).

sources.title: Wages: Operations manager, banking, credit and investment in Ontario (NOC 10021)
sources.supports: Ontario hourly wages low $38.46, median $58.97, high $96.15 (2023-2024).

assumptions: About 55% of files that reach analysis get a streamlined review, which senior analysts decide alone about 60% of the time and short-form memo (strong profiles up to about $500,000); the rest get a full spread, cash flow, guarantor and industry analysis. Without this lighter track, eight analysts could not handle 430 applications a month.

Valuation work by asset managers is documented in the value-equipment-and-set-residuals process; this workflow counts only the wait, so asset_manager carries 0 FTE here. The valuation_request output is linked with outcome 'any' because it is sent mid-process.

Organisation file ambiguity: approve-credit-above-authority says memos above a manager's limit go to the director of credit, while this process lists the director among its roles. Here the director approves within the director's own limit as part of underwriting, and only exposures above that go to the chief credit and risk officer or committee through approve-credit-above-authority.

Combined with small-ticket, about 30 files a month go to approve-credit-above-authority, below the organisation file's 60; the file's figure would be reached if part of the director's mid-ticket approvals were counted in that process instead.
Customer financials and asset valuations are inputs that arrive during a case, not case starts, so their trigger share is 0; the same for credit policy changes.
About 78% of fully reviewed files are approved, most with conditions; with early declines and withdrawals this gives roughly two thirds of decided files approved, in line with the organisation file.

Staffing: about 7.6 of 8 analysts, three quarters of the manager's time and a third of the director's time are on this process. Hands-on time implies slightly more analyst time than that; in practice analysts at this volume work long days or carry backlogs, and the organisation file looks about one mid-ticket analyst short for 430 applications a month.
Loaded costs are the organisation file's (2019-2022 wage times 1.35).
